conventions.convention: The thermodynamic-limit sequence starts at k=1; each state set is finite and nonempty, energies are finite, and weights are positive. The displayed normalization is free energy per physical volume; limiting existence and derivative interchange are not asserted.

Phase charts have positive temperature, real pressure, interior compositions and positive total amount. Numerical state coordinates are converted to physical SI coordinates by the declared unit map. An intensive branch additionally assumes chemical potentials independent of amount.

Coexistence means an attained global entropy maximum on the exact declared feasible set; intensive equalities require the corresponding exchange direction to be feasible bilaterally while other coordinates remain fixed.

Positive heat enters the system and positive work is done on it. The ideal pressure store supplies W_on=-p0 ΔV. The potential minimum concerns precisely the system projection of the same isolated-compound feasible set.

Stoichiometric columns are dimensionless, amounts and extents use moles, and a boundary equilibrium requires a separate boundary-inclusive model and finite C1 potential extension. Necessary optimality is nonnegative derivative on the feasible tangent cone; equality applies at an interior point.

Clapeyron jumps are β minus α. Same-tag local energy homogeneity is an additional hypothesis, the molar-volume jump must be nonzero, and latent heat is heat absorbed during the specified reversible α-to-β conversion.

Compact mixtures use countably additive probabilities on the relative Borel sigma algebra, without a completeness assumption. Generator coordinates are dimensionless, entropy is per mole, and every probability mixture at the prescribed barycenter must be physically admitted.

The reacting phase rule counts the local zero set of intensive coexistence-and-affinity equations, not the stable-coexistence set or phase amounts. There are C named species, P phases and R independent reaction directions; repeated affinity equations are counted once after imposing phase equalities.

load_bearing.statement: A phase branch supplies a C1 diffeomorphism from an open (T,p,x,m) chart to an open numerical equilibrium-state patch, reproducing its derivative-defined temperature, pressure and composition. An intensive branch additionally has chemical potentials independent of amount. Coexistence is an attained global entropy-maximizing feasible separated mixture.

At the stated attained global entropy maximum in smooth positive-temperature charts, bilateral energy exchange gives equal temperatures; bilateral volume exchange gives equal p/T; bilateral species exchange gives equal μ_j/T. The latter two give equal pressures and chemical potentials when energy exchange is also permitted.

Under the specified closed system record, isolated-compound extension, ideal reservoir and pressure-store assumptions, Φ=U+p0V−T0S does not increase. An attained global compound entropy maximum gives an attained global Φ minimum on the exact system projection of its feasible set.

For the stated two one-component branches, same-tag homogeneity, attained bilateral-exchange coexistence point and valid Gibbs charts, a nonzero molar-volume jump gives a unique local C1 equal-Gibbs graph with dp/dT=(sβ−sα)/(vβ−vα). The separately specified reversible ideal-reservoir conversion gives absorbed molar latent heat T(sβ−sα).

For nonempty compact K⊆R^d, d≥1, continuous entropy s, prescribed barycenter in conv K, and feasibility with entropy ∫s dP of every Borel probability at that barycenter, an entropy-maximizing probability exists with at most d+1 atoms.

A finite-state thermodynamic-limit contract specifies the sequence of finite nonempty state sets, finite energies, positive weights, volumes, amounts, boundary conditions, interactions and normalization; f(β,ρ)=lim F_k(β)/V_k is defined if this limit exists.

concerns.concern: F4 attributes 'T↦T^{-1} is smooth' to thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives. That supplier states continuity and differentiability with a first-derivative formula, not smoothness. Verification 2.1 supplies the required higher-order induction locally, so the example's conclusion remains supported; the supplier attribution should distinguish its first-derivative statement from the local smoothness deduction.

Proof 3.1 chooses a finite cover and representatives separately for each ε, then says 'the sequence obtained with ε=1/n converges'. Turning these existential finite constructions into a simultaneous sequence is an undeclared countable selection. The result needs no such selection: the displayed bound already shows that every neighborhood of y(P) intersects the closed convex hull. This is a short closure-argument gap, not a failure of the attainment claim.

alerts.finding: F2 says that def-borel-probability-law-on-a-polish-space and def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals supply that 'Borel probability measures integrate bounded Borel real functions, and the integral is linear.' The opened definitions define probability laws and integrability; neither establishes linearity. The theorem's deps omit thm-linearity-of-the-lebesgue-integral-on-l-one and an integral-order supplier, although Proof 4.1 uses integral approximation bounds and Proof 5.2 combines integrated mixtures. The ordinary published integral results establish these elementary uses, but the exact prerequisite attribution and declaration are incomplete.
